summary.whatChanges: Retypes `z.property()`/`z.properties()` to key off the schema's *input* type, widened to its primitive via a new `util.Widen` helper. Literal/enum schemas now type-check against plainly-typed properties without an `as string` cast. Docs, blog, and tests drop those casts and add type-level assertions. No runtime change.
behaviorChanges: `z.property("protocol", z.literal("https:"))` on a `URL` compiles without casting the literal to `string`
`z.properties({ ... })` accepts literal and enum schemas against widened primitive properties (e.g. `z.enum(["POST","PUT"])` for `Request.method`)
Property checks are now validated against the schema's input type, so a transforming schema (`z.string().transform(s => s.length)`) matches a `string` property, not a `number` one
Genuine type mismatches and unknown property keys still fail to compile
New exported type helper `util.Widen<T>` in zod core utils
risks: Switching from `core.output` to `core.input` can break existing TypeScript code that relied on a transforming schema's output type matching the property
Widening to primitives loosens type checking: a property typed as a narrow literal will now accept a mismatched literal schema of the same primitive
`Widen` does not handle symbol, union, or branded/template-literal types explicitly, so results may be surprising for those inputs
Change is type-only; no runtime validation tests confirm behavior is unchanged beyond existing cases
